E4 review searches, 28 Nov 2026, session web-search tool, mode "standard". Generic engineering terms only.

==================================================================================================== R01
QUERY: modular robot actuator forced air cooling thermal equivalent circuit maximum continuous current rated current
MODE: standard
---- tool output (verbatim) ----
Web search results for query: "modular robot actuator forced air cooling thermal equivalent circuit maximum continuous current rated current"

Links: [{"title":"Design of a Concentrically Stacked Modular Actuator with Forced Air Cooling for Multi-DOF Robotic Systems","url":"https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/11/11/2947/xml"},{"title":"Next Article in Journal","url":"https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/11/11/2947"},{"title":"www.osti.gov","url":"https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1369514"},{"title":"Active cooling system and method for robot manipulators","url":"https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/12343865"},{"title":"Design of a Concentrically Stacked Modular Actuator with Forced Air Cooling for Multi-DOF Robotic Systems","url":"https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/11/11/2947/review_report"},{"title":"Design of a Concentrically Stacked Modular Actuator with Forced Air Cooling for Multi-DOF Robotic Systems","url":"https://libmast.utm.my/Record/doaj.art-929c7fc97d57409f8e42aac672f57134"},{"title":"Linear actuator system","url":"https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/10626980"},{"title":"Modular rugged cooled actuator control system","url":"https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/12419017"},{"title":"Characterization and Thermal Management of a DC Motor-Driven Resonant Actuator for Miniature Mobile Robots with Oscillating Limbs","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.00798"},{"title":"improving robotic actuator torque density and efficiency through enhanced h 2016 01 01","url":"https://sandia.gov/research/publications/details/improving-robotic-actuator-torque-density-and-efficiency-through-enhanced-h-2016-01-01"}]

The best match is a 2018 *Energies* paper on a concentrically stacked modular (CoSMo) actuator with forced air cooling. Its prototype experiments found that the maximum continuous current that can be applied to the CoSMo actuator is up to about three times greater than the rated current in a forced air-cooling environment. The authors checked their thermal behavior with simulation of simplified model, and the paper's "Simplified thermal equivalent circuit" (STEC) abbreviation suggests that is the circuit in question. Adjacent actuator modules have twice the thermal capacitance and radiating area owing to the physical contact of the housings.

Other results are less direct. A separate DOE/OSTI report models motor coil temperature with a lumped heat transfer coefficient,Hm, and forced air cooling provides an 79% increase in heat transfer over the nominal design. A Sandia publication reports the same 79% figure for forced air and 107% with pumped water. An arXiv paper on a DC motor-driven resonant actuator uses a secondorder lumped parameter thermal circuit.

I did not find a source that defines the rated current for these actuators or gives a general formula relating forced-air cooling to maximum continuous current. The "about three times" figure comes from one prototype, so treat it as a case-specific result rather than a general rule.

QUERY: BLDC robot joint actuator winding to ambient thermal resistance K/W natural convection versus fan cooled airflow m/s measured
MODE: standard

Links: [{"title":"www.osti.gov","url":"https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1369514"},{"title":"Characterization and Thermal Management of a DC Motor-Driven Resonant Actuator for Miniature Mobile Robots with Oscillating Limbs","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.00798"},{"title":"jeffliulab.github.io","url":"https://jeffliulab.github.io/ai-notes/en/Robot_Engineering/08_Mechanical/%E6%95%A3%E7%83%AD%E4%B8%8E%E9%98%B2%E6%8A%A4/"},{"title":"DEV Community","url":"https://dev.to/peter_hong_44601bad413835/bldc-motor-torque-density-optimization-for-robot-joints-a-practical-design-guide-1fo9"},{"title":"par.nsf.gov","url":"https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10627793"},{"title":"Motor Thermal Model Interactive Calculator","url":"https://www.firgelliauto.com/es/blogs/calculators/motor-thermal-model-calculator"},{"title":"www.arxiv.org","url":"https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2509.23561"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.23561v1"},{"title":"Airflow Cooling Mechanism for High Power Density Permanent Magnet Motor","url":"https://ynu.repo.nii.ac.jp/record/2000254/files/Airflow_Cooling_Mechanism_for_High_Power-Density_Permanent_Magnet_Motor.pdf"},{"title":"Next Article in Journal","url":"https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/11/11/2947"}]

I ran one search. It did not turn up a measured pair of winding-to-ambient K/W values for a robot joint BLDC, one with natural convection and one with fan airflow at a stated m/s. The results are mostly general references and design notes.

- **Forced air vs. natural convection (OSTI/Sandia):** A motor thermal study reports that forced air raised heat transfer about 79% over its nominal design, and forced water about 107%. It gives thermal resistance terms (coil, iron, housing, environment) in K/W but does not tie them to a specific airflow speed. Forced convection increases heat transfer over the nominal design by79%with forced air and 107%with pumped water.
- **Convection coefficients (Firgelli calculator):** The page gives typical h ranges, roughly 5–25 W/(m²·K) for still air and 25–250 W/(m²·K) for forced air, and states that forced cooling can reduce thermal resistance by an order of magnitude. It also gives typical winding-to-ambient values of 2-5 °C/W for smaller motors and 0.5-2 °C/W for larger motors with forced cooling. These are generic figures, not joint-specific measurements.
- **Robot-joint thermal model (arXiv 2002.00798):** This paper models case-to-air convection as free convection, which it describes as a worst case where the air is stagnant. It also notes that higher rotor speeds increase forced convection in the air gap. Its thermal resistance values are for a resonant actuator, not a rotary joint.
- **Forced-air modular actuator (MDPI Energies 2018, 11(11):2947):** This paper on a forced-air-cooled actuator for multi-DOF robots says the benefit of forced cooling depends on the thermal resistance and thermal capacitance of the winding and housing. I did not retrieve its measured K/W values or airflow speeds.
- **Design blog (DEV Community):** One post lists a housing-to-ambient resistance of 1.2 °C/W for a robot joint prototype, but it provides no airflow or natural-convection comparison, and its source is unverified.

For measured data at specific airflow speeds, the MDPI actuator paper and the robot-joint thermal papers cited in it are the most likely sources. I did not open them, so I have not verified their numbers.

Links: [{"title":"Design and Characterization of 3D Printed, Open-Source Actuators for Legged Locomotion","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.12395"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.12395v1"},{"title":"Design and Characterization of 3D Printed, Open-Source Actuators for Legged Locomotion","url":"https://cdnjs.deepai.org/publication/design-and-characterization-of-3d-printed-open-source-actuators-for-legged-locomotion"},{"title":"Legged high-dexterity self-balancing capable robot actor","url":"https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/11247738"},{"title":"High-torque actuator for legged robots","url":"https://discourse.odriverobotics.com/t/high-torque-actuator-for-legged-robots/776"},{"title":"Design and characterization of 3d printed, open-source actuators for legged locomotion","url":"https://flounder-plantain-pba9.squarespace.com/publications-archive/design-and-characterization-of-3d-printed-open-source-actuators-for-legged-locomotion"},{"title":"export.arxiv.org","url":"https://export.arxiv.org/pdf/2503.14255"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.14255v2"},{"title":"← all papers · overview","url":"https://awesomepapers.io/robotics/papers/2202.12395"},{"title":"discussion 110527","url":"https://hackaday.io/project/159404-opentorque-actuator/discussion-110527"}]

I ran one search. The top hit is the most relevant: Urs et al., "Design and Characterization of 3D Printed, Open-Source Actuators for Legged Locomotion" (IROS 2022). It describes two 3D-printed quasi-direct-drive actuators and a fan-based thermal solution. The snippets I got don't include the thermal resistance value or the continuous current rating, so I can't give you those numbers from this search.

- **Cooling design:** The paper says passive cooling through plastic or aluminum heatsinks wasn't enough, so the authors added active cooling. Two small centrifugal fans sit on the side of each actuator and push air through ducts over the motor windings and rotor. [arxiv.org/pdf/2202.12395](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.12395)
- **Why fans:** The authors note that legged actuators often hold torque without rotating, so driving fans with the main motor won't work, and dedicated fans are needed. [arxiv.org/pdf/2202.12395](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.12395)
- **Thermal result:** The abstract says the thermal solution nearly doubles the thermally driven torque limits of the plastic design. [deepai.org mirror](https://cdnjs.deepai.org/publication/design-and-characterization-of-3d-printed-open-source-actuators-for-legged-locomotion)
- **Other context:** A 2025 quadruped paper (arXiv 2503.14255) uses 3D-printed and laser-cut QDD actuators with heatsinks for thermal management, but its snippets don't give thermal resistance or current figures.

To get the exact thermal resistance and continuous current numbers, the next step is to open the full Urs et al. PDF (arXiv 2202.12395), probably in its thermal design and characterization sections.
